markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors specific recent connections over broad similarity; test context dependence without assuming older interactions are irrelevant. (2) Existing margins depend on score scale and sampled negatives; matched ranks complement them. (3) Compatibility and replacement needs remain unknown; title/description evidence cannot establish ownership or practical fit.

**Related work.** (1) NextItNet’s receptive field depends on every temporal convolution, not block count [1,5]. (2) Sampled ranking can reverse comparisons; diagnostics cannot replace pinned validation HR@10 [2]. (3) Repeated validation selection introduces bias [3]. (4) Adaptive long/short fusion already exists [6–8], reducing the gate’s novelty. These support three directions: causal context auditing, economical adaptive context, and evidence-grounded feedback annotation.

## Framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Intervention | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context dependence | Paired prefix target ranks | Recent/old deletion and shuffling | Dependence does not establish intent |
| Adaptive context | Recent versus full-context features | One jointly trained residual gate | Boundary effects can imitate context effects |
| Feedback grounding | Exact title/description spans | Supported/contradicted/unknown labels | Similarity cannot prove compatibility |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality / future potential / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Matched context audit: 4/7/3.** Freeze NextItNet; compare equal-count recent/old deletions using fixed candidates [1,2]. Positive: inexpensive dependence evidence. Negative: unrealistic perturbations limit interpretation.
2. **Recent-context residual gate: 3/6/7 — selected conditionally.** Share one NextItNet across full and cropped histories [1,6–8]. Positive: directly tests adaptive recency. Negative: established fusion, possible redundant branches, and expensive per-target crops.
3. **Evidence-grounded feedback audit: 4/6/4.** Annotate recommendation–history relations using text spans and unknowns [4]. Positive: exposes unsupported compatibility claims. Negative: twenty-user coverage is exploratory and does not optimize ranking directly.

## Selected algorithm

First derive `R = 1 + Σ(k−1)d` from every temporal convolution; exclude shortcuts and 1×1 layers. Verify causal padding, channel-only normalization, and final nonpadding readout. With compatible boundaries and deterministic inference, full and last-eight outputs coincide when `R≤8`; then reject the eight-item gate experiment as redundant. For `R>8`, proceed only after controlled prefix perturbations distinguish older-context influence from padding artifacts.

For each category, share all encoder/embedding parameters. At each supervised position, independently crop its causal prefix to eight items, left-pad, and encode. Compute `g=sigmoid(MLP([h_full,h_recent]))`; score `LayerNorm(h_full+g*(h_recent−h_full))` using the baseline scorer and loss. This remains one jointly trained network/checkpoint.

Independent windows repeat computation; unfolding does not eliminate it. Specify gate dimensions, initialization, normalization, padding treatment, and crop semantics in the saved configuration. Compare against normalization-matched full-only and fixed-average controls before claiming adaptive selection [8]. Keep the hypothesis set small: controls consume the shared search budget.

Preserve routing, `GAGC_DATA_DIR`, ModelView/diagnostic contracts, predictor reconstruction, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and maximum 200 epochs with 200 batches/epoch. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; report no unmeasured gains. Gates may exploit popularity or history length; training-only strata and matched perturbations expose such shortcuts without establishing intent.

References: [1] NextItNet; [2] On Sampled Metrics; [3] Cawley–Talbot; [4] Product Relationships; [5] Microsoft/RecBole implementations; [6] SLi-Rec; [7] CLSR; [8] TLSRec. Links appear in related_work.

idea.description: Conditionally test a recent-context residual gate inside one NextItNet model per category. One shared causal convolutional encoder processes full prefixes and independently cropped recent prefixes; a jointly trained gate combines their features before the existing item scorer. Retain the corrected baseline if the eight-item branch is redundant or the experiment exceeds the remaining search budget.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests specific recent interests sometimes lose to broad historical relevance, but does not demonstrate stale history or identifiable intent. The proposal tests adaptive context emphasis. Established long/short interest fusion limits originality, and the experiment is meaningful only if the baseline receptive field reaches beyond the recent window and measured branch differences reflect historical input rather than padding behavior.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from the supplied corrected NextItNet baseline without inspecting other trials. Compute R=1+sum((k_l-1)*d_l) over every stride-one temporal convolution, including both convolutions when present in a residual block. Verify left-only padding, no future-token influence, position-local normalization, and matching deterministic train/predict feature semantics. Fix W=8 for this hypothesis; if R<=8 and compatible boundary semantics make branches identical, reject this variant without searching alternative windows against validation. If R>8, perturb only interactions preceding the recent window and separately test padding/boundary effects before interpreting branch differences. Neither nonzero padding states nor full/crop differences alone establish useful historical information. Preserve chronological order, padding conventions, and every per-target crop boundary; masking a final feature cannot remove earlier information already propagated through layers. Share all backbone and item-embedding parameters. Set a reproducible gate: concatenate two D-dimensional features, apply Linear(2D,1) with zero-initialized weights and bias, then sigmoid; broadcast the scalar over channels. Use LayerNorm(D) with eps=1e-5 and affine parameters initialized to one and zero. This initially averages branches before normalization. Preserve the baseline scorer, objective, optimizer, sampling, and other hyperparameters, recording their supplied values rather than inventing replacements. Return B×L×D from log2feats; only valid supervised positions require recent-window evaluation during training. For left-padded nonempty histories use the final nonpadding position, ordinarily index L-1, never count-1; explicitly handle empty histories using the baseline convention. Full-catalog inference needs only one full-prefix and one recent-prefix feature per user. Training needs a distinct recent crop for each supervised position, potentially multiplying convolution work by roughly W; Tensor.unfold alone does not remove that arithmetic. Estimate runtime before committing, and use activation checkpointing or chunked windows if necessary. Chunked gradient accumulation must normalize each chunk by the total number of valid targets and take one optimizer step per original batch; shared full-feature graphs require retention or recomputation, so chunking alone does not guarantee bounded memory. Retain sample_batch, ModelView, view.model as the actual module, view.item_emb, predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Report unavailable diagnostics as null with counts and definitions. Use only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; no ratings, reviews, unavailable categories, inferred simulator traits, or unsupported compatibility claims. Preserve splits, all four category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and 200 batches per epoch. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category. Embed identical architecture, padding rules, gate, normalization, crop length, and checkpoint keys in the predictor writer. No separate transition/popularity scores, checkpoint averaging, or independent predictors. Predeclare the gate experiment and, only within the remaining budget, normalization-matched full-only and fixed-average controls. Short-only, global-scalar, tuned-fixed-interpolation, and parameter-matched full-only controls are useful subsequent experiments; do not claim adaptive selection without adequate controls. Choose deployed models using only the host's pinned macro validation HR@10, keeping candidates and evaluator unchanged. Training-prefix perturbations and twenty-user full-catalog feedback remain explanatory evidence. Report category/history-length/target-popularity strata with counts using training-derived bins; these describe observed behavior, not latent traits. Paired user bootstrap intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty, not seed variability or adaptive selection bias.
idea.pseudocode:
Derive R from every temporal convolution in the corrected NextItNet.
Verify causality, normalization axes, padding semantics, and final nonpadding readout.
Set W=8; predeclare this single gate hypothesis.
If R<=W and compatible deterministic branch outputs coincide:
    reject this redundant variant; retain the corrected baseline.
Otherwise distinguish older-input influence from padding/boundary effects.
For each category independently:
    initialize one shared NextItNet F and its baseline item embedding/scorer
    initialize G=Linear(2D,1) to zero; initialize LayerNorm(D) conventionally
    for each baseline training batch, within the fixed epoch/batch limits:
        H_full = F(sequence)
        for each valid supervised position (b,t):
            prefix = sequence[b,:t+1]
            crop = left_pad(last_8_nonpadding_items(prefix))
            h_recent[b,t] = final_nonpadding_feature(F(crop))
        g = sigmoid(G(concat(H_full, h_recent)))
        H = LayerNorm(H_full + g * (h_recent - H_full))
        optimize the baseline loss on valid positions using baseline negatives
        use checkpointing/chunking only with equivalent loss normalization
    save one joint checkpoint plus complete architecture configuration
    generate a predictor reconstructing the identical network and crop semantics
At inference:
    encode the full history and its last-eight crop with the shared F
    fuse their final nonpadding features using the trained gate and normalization
    score requested items with the baseline scorer
Compare the predefined variant and available matched controls through pinned macro validation HR@10.
Use fixed-candidate training-prefix perturbations only as diagnostics; report no unmeasured improvement.

originality.positive: A shared causal convolutional implementation with explicit receptive-field and boundary checks gives a precise, falsifiable context-selection experiment.
originality.negative: Adaptive long/short interest fusion is established in SLi-Rec, CLSR, and TLSRec; sharing NextItNet weights does not itself establish a substantial new contribution.

future_potential.positive: Controlled evidence could motivate economical context adaptation and clarify which history-length or popularity groups benefit.
future_potential.negative: The gate may be redundant, exploit simple shortcuts, or fail to improve ranking; interactions alone cannot resolve practical fit, ownership, or replacement intent.

code_difficulty.positive: The gate and scorer changes are small and reuse the baseline's learned components.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact per-position crop semantics, repeated convolution work, gradient-memory management, boundary verification, and matching embedded inference make the complete experiment substantially harder than a two-pass description suggests.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal dilated convolutions and residual blocks for sequential recommendation.
Supplies the backbone preserved by the proposed shared-parameter context gate.
limitations: Actual receptive field depends on the implemented temporal convolutions and dilation schedule.
Sequence dependence alone cannot establish current purpose, compatibility, or replacement need.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can yield inconsistent comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not make training-prefix diagnostics or full-catalog feedback interchangeable with the pinned sampled validation benchmark.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated optimization of a selection criterion biases performance assessment.
Motivates a small predefined hypothesis set under the shared search budget.
limitations: Does not estimate task-specific selection bias; bootstrap intervals do not correct repeated validation selection.

related_work.title: Inferring Networks of Substitutable and Complementary Products
contributions: Distinguishes substitute and complement relationships, motivating precise feedback annotation.
limitations: Product relationships do not establish ownership, replacement intent, or instance-specific compatibility.
Its data assumptions must not introduce unavailable reviews or metadata into this task.

related_work.title: Microsoft Recommenders NextItNet implementation
contributions: Illustrates a bottleneck residual implementation with one temporal convolution per block.
Exposes convolution biases and channel-wise normalization relevant to causal locality and padding effects.
limitations: Does not establish the supplied baseline's architecture; its actual convolution list must determine R.
Zero input padding does not guarantee zero hidden states at padded positions.

related_work.title: RecBole NextItNet implementation
contributions: Illustrates residual blocks with temporal convolutions at dilations d and 2d.
Demonstrates why block count alone cannot determine receptive-field span.
limitations: Architecture-specific deductions cannot be transferred to the host baseline without checking its definitions.

related_work.title: SLi-Rec: Sequential Recommendation with User Memory Networks
contributions: Combines long-term preferences and a time/content-aware short-term representation through adaptive attention.
Establishes prior art for context-dependent long/short interest fusion.
limitations: Its recurrent architecture and inputs differ from a shared NextItNet encoder.
Its results do not establish gains for this benchmark or isolate the proposed crop semantics.

related_work.title: CLSR: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Disentangles long- and short-term interests using contrastive supervision and adaptively aggregates them.
limitations: The proposed gate lacks equivalent disentanglement supervision.
Separate context inputs alone do not guarantee distinct or interpretable interests.

related_work.title: TLSRec
contributions: Provides relevant comparisons between adaptive fusion, equal averaging, and alternative attention mechanisms.
Motivates a fixed-average control for the proposed gate.
limitations: Reported improvements do not establish adaptive context selection in NextItNet.
Normalization and capacity controls remain necessary for attributing any observed gain.

related_work.title: PyTorch Tensor.unfold documentation
contributions: Describes overlapping window views useful for constructing per-target recent histories.
limitations: Reshaping may materialize data, and a view does not eliminate repeated neural computation.

related_work.title: PyTorch activation checkpointing documentation
contributions: Documents a recomputation-based approach to reducing retained activation memory.
limitations: Adds computation and requires attention to deterministic recomputation; it provides no task-specific throughput guarantee.
